properties.statement: {server} never writes {page-file}; while it queues, refuses, restarts or takes an ack the file's bytes stay as they were.
A change id is an integer one above every integer id in the pending and applied files, also after a restart; a refused post uses no id.
A restart on the same page prints the same url as long as {url-file} stays and the port is free.
No pending line is printed before the quiet window has passed since the newest change, and one line is printed for the whole burst.
A reload event is sent only for page content that stayed the same for a whole 0.5 s poll and holds {runtime}'s closing marker.
An ack sends a changes event and never a reload; only a change of {page-file} reloads an open page.
{server} listens on 127.0.0.1 only; no other address of the machine, ::1 included, accepts a connection on its port.
No route answers with {url-file}, anything under changes/ or {history-folder}, or a file whose path has a piece opening with a dot.
Every file of {history-folder} has no write bit: its mode is 0444.
A change recorded on a served page is either answered by {server} or stays in the tab's unsent list, across reloads, until {server} answers.
The open panel and a typed draft are the same after the reload an applied edit causes.
A badge is updated in place and never rebuilt, so a redraw between a press and its release does not drop the click.
A page with missing or broken blocks, a throwing pageRender or no sessionStorage still loads without an uncaught error, with window.pageData as {}.
The copy of {runtime} inside {starter} equals assets/page-runtime.js stripped; {connector} on the starter writes nothing.
Each entry id is used once in the whole threads block, and a session entry replies to an entry of its own thread.
Only {session} writes threads and page data in the file; {runtime} and {server} only read them.
A page lives outside every repository, since {server} creates changes/, {history-folder} and {url-file} beside it; nothing in the folder checks this.
A post's Content-Length is 1,000,000 at most and a comment's text 4000 characters at most; a longer one is answered 400.
The three Python scripts and the two fixture runners import only the standard library and no other script.
Nobody but {person} and {session} learns the url: anyone on the machine who has it can read the page, read the queue and, with the right Origin header, post and ack.
{session} has python3, curl and a Monitor that runs a long command and wakes on each stdout line; {browser-run} has node, Playwright and macOS on arm64.
{browser} adds the Origin header to {runtime}'s same-origin POST by itself; {runtime} sets only Content-Type.
An anchor id, a change's target and a thread key match [\w.:-]{1,80} in full: 1 to 80 letters, digits or _.:-.
A person's entry keeps its change id and by person; a session's reply takes the id `<comment id>`.`<k>`, by session and replies_to the comment's id.
A fixture page is named follows-`<case>`.html or break-`<rule>`.html; the name alone fixes the verdict {replay-check} expects.
A history copy is named `<local time as %Y%m%dT%H%M%S%f>`-`<first 12 hex of the sha256>`.html, so names sort by time.
Every sessionStorage key is page-changes:`<location.pathname>`:`<name>`, so two pages of one origin do not share state.
Every stdout line of {server} opens with `page-changes `, then `url:` or `pending`.
A Python script answers a call it cannot read, --help included, with its docstring on stderr, nothing on stdout and exit 2, and changes nothing.
{keeper} run once at start and the one {watcher} runs are one procedure on one memory, so a version seen at start is neither copied twice nor reloaded for.

SKILL.md's {rule-valid-blocks} rule reads, as stored, write a raw less-than sign inside the blocks as the same raw sign, while the checker's escape rule forbids a raw one and says to write \u003c; this contract follows the checker.

{connector}'s docstring says `updated <page>` is printed when an older copy was replaced; the code prints it whenever the markers are found, also when nothing was written, and {browser-run} relies on that.
SKILL.md says a thread lives under its anchor's id only; the checker also takes a key that is an id inside page data, and SKILL.md does not say so.
The folder names {session}'s Monitor and its longest timeout and defines neither; how a Monitor is armed and how long it lasts is settled {outside}.
No source says how k in a reply id `<comment id>`.`<k>` is chosen; {browser-run} uses 1 for the first reply.
Nothing says what a session does with an exported changes.json; its changes carry no id, and no script reads the file.
A change {server} refuses disappears from {person}'s view; no source says whether {person} should be told.
SKILL.md describes a data change as carrying payload.path and payload.value; {server} queues a data change with any object as payload, an empty one included.
The latest data change per target and path is not defined further; the queue's order and rising ids are the only order the sources give.
{server} defines GET and POST only; what another method gets is left to Python's http.server and was not run.
